_comment: Fragment 54 — D-100: the operating model is Scrum; C-20 withdrawn; Phases 2 and 3 opened. Merged 2026-08-22.

nodes.label: D-100 — The Operating Model Is Scrum, Not a Stage Gate
nodes.description: The project is approved and standing. The spec-acceptance boundary exists only to let a working lane proceed, not to authorize existence. The cycle across the three lanes is continuous, and feedback against running work goes to the top of the backlog without halting the work or invalidating the spec.
nodes.rationale: Gaps close progressively through spec refinement. The governing phrases are the project's own: keep things simple and practical, and start where you are, which the sprint plan already cites.

nodes.label: Competent Answers to the Wrong Question
nodes.description: Phase closure conditions, exits, a deadlock and serialization enforcement were each a reasonable response to a stage-gate model that the project does not use. The symptoms were visible across three passes and were read as separate defects rather than one mismatch.
nodes.rationale: The common cause is not insufficient rigour. Lane A kept adding governance where the answer was less of it.

nodes.label: Only Someone Outside the Model Can Say the Model Is Wrong
nodes.description: Three consecutive passes had a Lane A rule corrected by the Judge rather than by a control. A critic pass checks work against its own model's rules, so it cannot detect that the model itself is mismatched to how the project runs.
nodes.rationale: This is the strongest evidence yet that the Judge could not have been a fourth agent. An agent inside the same model would share the mismatch.

nodes.label: C-20 Withdrawn — a Control Against the Model
nodes.description: The check was to enforce that lanes act strictly one phase at a time. Under a continuous cycle it would fire on the normal case, which is the property that makes a control get ignored. What survives from the finding that opened it is satisfied by the phase register plus the handoff status field.
nodes.rationale: Withdrawn rather than deferred, because deferral implies it becomes correct later and it does not. A control that enforces the opposite of how the project works is worse than a missing one.

nodes.label: The Channel Already Is the Backlog
nodes.description: Entries are raised by a working lane, dispositioned by the orchestration lane, and ordered by whoever is refining. New feedback goes to the top because information about running work is the most perishable in the cycle. A full backlog is not a defect.
nodes.rationale: No separate backlog artifact is created. A second file listing these entries would restate them, and restatements drift, which is the mistake this ruling corrects repeated in miniature.

nodes.label: Permission to Proceed Granted
nodes.description: Both working phases are open under the standing project approval. The application lane starts with the thirteen unimplemented configuration rows, then the flags module; the CI lane has its two workflow items, one still waiting on a repository-settings act.
nodes.rationale: The earlier commit that ran ahead of a recorded permission is reclassified as a process-recording gap inside an approved project, whose remedy is a backlog entry rather than the phase-validity crisis three passes treated it as.
